trips.route_note: Take a train from Colombo Fort (about 2 to 2.5 hours, the coastal line) or an express bus via the Southern Expressway (about 2 hours), then take a tuk-tuk or walk about 15 to 20 minutes from the station to Galle Fort.
trips.why: The coastal train takes about 2 hours and reaches Galle station close to the old fort, so it beats the 2h21m bus.
know: Galle Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is best explored on foot.
The coastal line is often crowded, so arrive early for a seat.

bus.via: Colombo Bastian Mawatha Bus Terminal to Kandy Good Shed Bus Station

trips.route_note: Take a direct train from Colombo Fort (about 3 hours through the hill country) and then a tuk-tuk into the centre, which is a few minutes from Kandy station.
see: Temple of the Tooth (Sri Dalada Maligawa)
Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya (short tuk-tuk ride)
quests: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
trips.why: The hill-country train takes about 2h31m, is scenic, and ends a few minutes by tuk-tuk from the centre, far faster than the 4h10m bus.
know: The Temple of the Tooth is the main sight and is a sacred site, so dress modestly.
Book reserved seats ahead on the hill-country train, especially for the day trip.

trips.route_note: Take a train from Colombo Fort to Negombo station (about 1 hour) or a bus from the Pettah bus station (about 1 to 1.5 hours), then walk or take a tuk-tuk to the fish market and beach.
trips.why: The bus takes 55 minutes from Pettah, quicker than the 1h21m train, and the sights are a short walk or tuk-tuk ride from the stop.
know: The fish market is liveliest in the morning.
Negombo works well as a short half-day trip rather than a full day.
